subject: MAP: Technical evaluation — VividRx benchmark & responsibilities
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@vividrx.com>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa@vividrx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-25T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: MAP: Technical evaluation — VividRx benchmark & responsibilities

Hi Samir / Alyssa —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. As promised, I attached a first-pass MAP focused on the Technical Evaluation milestone. High level ask: confirm the milestone owners below and the target close date so we can lock resources on our side.

Quick summary of proposed technical evaluation milestones (high level):
- Milestone 1: Sample data & access (owner: VividRx) — deliver anonymized test corpus + data schema by 2026-09-02.
- Milestone 2: Baseline benchmark run (owner: Redwood) — run on customer's sample and provide baseline accuracy/latency/cost report within 7 business days of data receipt.
- Milestone 3: Model shortlist + quantization trial (owner: Redwood + VividRx) — shortlist 3 models, run quantized inference permutations, report throughput & per-inference cost.
- Milestone 4: Latency stress tests & SLO validation (owner: Redwood) — p50/p95/p99 latency across expected payloads and concurrency profiles. Target p95 < 250ms for typical clinical query (see details below).
- Milestone 5: Security & compliance evidence (owner: VividRx + Redwood) — exchange SOC2 artifact pointers and confirm audit log access for trial.

Proposed target for MAP completion / decision: 2026-10-15. If VividRx needs earlier, flag now and we’ll prioritize.

Benchmark success criteria (draft):
- Functional: match or exceed current rule-based baseline on the task F1 by +6 points (on agreed eval set).
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 250ms for short queries (<= 128 tokens); p50 <= 90ms.
- Cost: estimated inference cost <= $0.045 per 1k input tokens (pre-quantization baseline) or demonstrable cost improvement with quantization.
- Stability: no catastrophic regression across top-5 prompts in held-out set.

Model shortlist (initial): Llama 2 70B (quantized variants), Mistral Instruct 7B, Falcon 40B-instruct. We’ll propose a Redwood-verified perf profile for each and run at least two precision modes (fp16 and 4-bit quant).

Attachments: VividRx_MAP-draft-v1.xlsx (MAP table + milestones) and eval-bench-template.csv (sample benchmark harness + metric columns).

Next steps: can you confirm owners and the sample data ETA? I’ll hand this to Marissa to scope the run and Ben to prepare the cost model.

Thanks —
Jonas
Jonas Weber | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | jonas.weber@redwood.com
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@vividrx.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@vividrx.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-25T12:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation — VividRx benchmark & responsibilities

Jonas — thanks, this looks like a solid starting point. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Sample data: we can provide a 10k-record anonymized export covering the three primary clinical intents by 2026-09-01 (not 09-02) — is that acceptable? We’ll include a mapping doc for any protected fields redaction.
2) Latency targets: p95 <= 250ms is reasonable; we’d prefer a goal of p95 <= 200ms for production. Can Redwood note both target and stretch goal in the MAP?
3) Compliance: we need visibility into request-level audit logs during the trial (not just aggregated metrics). Will Redwood enable a read-only log stream or S3 export?

Also important for procurement: we'll need a one-page summary of expected cost at three traffic tiers (1k, 10k, 100k monthly inference requests) using the benchmarked models. Can Ben include that in the next update?

Finally, target decision date: we’re aiming to finalize a vendor by 2026-10-10 to align with an upcoming Q4 initiative. Can the MAP be adjusted to that close date?

Samir
Samir Patel | Director of AI Platforms, VividRx
samir.patel@vividrx.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@vividrx.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-25T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation — VividRx benchmark & responsibilities

Thanks Samir — and noted on the earlier data ETA and decision date. I’ve incorporated Samir's asks into the attached MAP (v1.1) and added some execution notes below.

Execution notes and refined success criteria (Redwood delivery commitments):
- Data intake & validation (owner: VividRx for delivery; Redwood for schema validation). We’ll run a quick ingestion check within 48 hours of receipt to confirm labeling and tokenization assumptions.
- Baseline run: We will run the three shortlisted models against the provided eval set and produce the accuracy (F1), latency (p50/p95/p99), and cost-per-1k-tokens estimates. Expected duration: 3 business days from validated data.
- Latency measurement details: runs will use a standard payload distribution (short: <=128 tokens, medium: 128-512, long: >512). We’ll report per-bucket p50/p95/p99 and tail behavior with concurrency = 1, 5, 20.
- Target vs stretch: we’ll capture both your requested target (p95 <= 200ms) and a stretch (p95 <= 150ms) in the report so stakeholders can evaluate tradeoffs.
- Quantization & perf: for each model we’ll test fp16 baseline and 4-bit quant (both static and dynamic if supported) and surface any quality delta vs baseline.

Dependencies / risks we flagged:
- Full fidelity tokens: if export strips punctuation or anonymization alters tokenization, results may diverge; we’ll highlight tokenization drift in the report.
- Test environment parity: the trial will run on Redwood Dedicated nodes in us-west; production region parity may affect latency.
- Audit log access: we can provide S3 request-level logs for the trial. We’ll confirm format and retention window up front.

Owners (final):
- VividRx: Samir (data export + stakeholder alignment), Alyssa (clinical SME for eval set)
- Redwood: Marissa (benchmark execution / reporting), Ben (cost model & commercial), Jonas (overall MAP coordination)

I attached MAP-v1.1 with the updated dates (target decision 2026-10-10) and a short runbook. Please review and let us know if anything else should be added.

Best —
Marissa Cole
Technical Program Manager, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Attachment: VividRx_MAP-draft-v1.1.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation — VividRx benchmark & responsibilities

Samir / team — quick note from commercial side.

I’ll prepare the three-tier cost projection (1k/10k/100k reqs) using the benchmark outputs and include sensitivity for quantized vs fp16 runs. To do that I need one confirm: will the eval traffic pattern be mostly short queries (<=128 tokens) or mixed? If mixed, please indicate approximate distribution (short/medium/long).

Also: procurement will want an initial SOW stub for the trial (1 month) and a pricing breakout for Dedicated vs Hosted (we can provide both). I’ll draft and share by EOD Monday (2026-08-30) assuming we get the sample data on 09-01.

Ben
Ben Carter | Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: MAP: Technical evaluation — VividRx benchmark & responsibilities

Thanks all — quick answers:
- Data ETA: confirming 2026-09-01 (we’ll upload to the provided S3 bucket and share access links).
- Traffic profile: estimated 70% short (<=128), 25% medium (128-512), 5% long (>512).
- Audit logs: we appreciate S3 export — we'll confirm ACLs and retention requirements in a separate email to Marissa.
- Decision date: confirmed 2026-10-10. If Redwood can produce the benchmark report + cost model by 2026-09-09 (7 business days after data delivery), that works for us.

Samir
